name: Hologram AI kernel
purpose: Decides what Hologram AI may load and run. A request names one decision in its first byte and carries that decision's numbers; the answer is the verdict. Thirty-nine decisions: the next step of the journey (1), whether a model may proceed (2), whether a stage plan is right (3), the quantisation tier (4), whether a buffer is admitted (5), whether a tensor's byte range is valid (6), whether a trim of the conversation is right (7), the next attention cache size (8), a turn's token budget (9), whether an ONNX graph may be imported (10), the size a dimension is bound to (11), which backend can run the model (12), how long one block of weights is (13), whether a token is the first of the highest scores (14), whether a token lies in the penalty window (15), whether a speculative commit is the right size (16) what a quantisation code stands for (17), whether an ONNX operator's name is one the engine runs (18), whether a model's family and shape are (19), how long a 4-bit ONNX weight's parts are (20), which precision fits (21), whether the model runs on WebGPU, on the CPU or not at all (22), whether a span of one of a model's files may be read (23), what each of a model's files is called (24), whether generation stops (25), whether a cached block is dropped (26), whether a computed prefix may be reused (27), whether a model's manifest is satisfied (28), whether a sum of products is held exactly (29), where a run gives the same answer again (30), whether replaying an answer confirms its receipt (31), whether opening part of a past answer shows the value that produced it (32), whether a prefix computed elsewhere may be reused (33), whether one block's claimed sum of products is exact (34), whether a label is a BLAKE3 address (35), whether a run may start with no floating point in it (36), what integers a stored q4 byte, half, bfloat16 or binary32 holds (37), whether a step may narrow a value with its declared width and bound (38) and whether a partial sum of a row is exact after its next terms (39). Anything else answers invalid request.
placeholder: hex: followed by the decision's bytes

promise.headline: Admits a buffer exactly when its label and its length are the ones expected.
promise.detail: A buffer's label is the BLAKE3 hash of its bytes. The kernel compares all 32 bytes of the expected and observed labels and the declared and observed lengths, and admits only when every one is equal.

claim: KN-05: a buffer is admitted exactly when its expected and observed labels are equal and its declared and observed lengths are equal.

proposition.name: Admitted
proposition.text:
Admitted claim :=
  SameLabel claim.expected claim.observed
  /\ claim.declaredLength = claim.observedLength

SameLabel left right :=
  left.w0 = right.w0 /\ left.w1 = right.w1 /\ left.w2 = right.w2 /\ left.w3 = right.w3
proposition.plain: The observed label is the expected label, word for word, and the observed length is the declared length.
